title: Map Pixels to Ground Distance Converter
description: Convert a pixel measurement on a map into ground distance with Map Pixels to Ground Distance — zoom and latitude aware. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a runway measuring 830 pixels in a zoom-17 screenshot at 45° latitude is 830 × 0.845 ≈ 700 metres of real concrete — measured off a picture, honestly.
quick_answer: Map Pixels to Ground Distance converts a pixel count measured on a Web Mercator map into the ground distance it represents at that zoom and latitude. Enter pixels, zoom and latitude and read metres or feet — screenshot measurement with the scale arithmetic done properly.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
Ground distance = pixels × metres-per-pixel at the stated zoom and latitude, under the Web Mercator tile standard.
Which map standard does it use?
Slippy-map Web Mercator — the standard your screenshots come from.
Can I use this in production GIS?
For measurement estimates from rendered maps, yes with the resize caveat. Production measurement belongs on vector data or imagery with ground control.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — the frame GPS produces and web maps consume.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — resolution is not accuracy; the precision tools on this site price each decimal place in metres.
My screenshot is from a retina screen.
Retina captures double the pixels per map pixel: halve your count (or double the rate) before converting.
The image was emailed and shrunk.
Then pixel truth died in transit — recover scale from any known-length feature in frame and calibrate manually; the converter prices counts, not miracles.
Feet and yards?
Outputs include imperial — playing fields come out in yards when you need them to.
Curved features?
Sum segment pixel counts along the curve, then convert the total — Mercator's local scale treats the path's pixels uniformly at one latitude.
Latitude varies along my feature?
Use the mid-latitude's rate; long north-south features accumulate small scale drift the geodesic tools avoid entirely.
